growth_thesis.basis: Growth rate and ratios are stated in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A. The condition that bookings must stay above revenue is inferred from the book-to-bill definition.
growth_thesis.claim: Driver 1: Commercial IT consulting. Consulting revenue rose 14.4 percent in the last fiscal year. For this to continue, bookings must keep exceeding revenue: the trailing-twelve-month book-to-bill was 1.1 to 1 at the latest quarter, but the third-quarter ratio alone was 0.9 to 1.
quotes: Commercial Segment consulting revenues were $1.3 billion, up 14.4 percent year-over-year.

growth_thesis.basis: Assignment decline and nine-month commercial growth are stated in the cited items. That assignment must stabilise is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition: the shrinking assignment business must stop offsetting consulting growth. Assignment revenue fell 13.8 percent in the last fiscal year. Commercial segment revenue was up only 0.3 percent over nine months, so total growth needs assignment to stabilise.
quotes: reflecting continued softness in the portions of the Commercial Segment Business that are more sensitive to changes in the macroeconomic cycles

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A tables. The replenishment condition is inferred from the book-to-bill definition.
growth_thesis.claim: Driver 2: Federal Government segment. Third-quarter revenue was up 3.8 percent. Continued growth requires awards to replenish backlog, but trailing-twelve-month new awards were 1,049.2 against 1,158.6 a year earlier (table in millions), with a 0.9 to 1 book-to-bill. Contract backlog was 2,943.4 (table in millions).
quotes: Federal Government Segment revenues were approximately 30 percent of total revenues and were up 3.8 percent year-over-year.

growth_thesis.basis: Cash paid, goodwill and debt are in the statements. Quinnox is named in the 10-Q. The funding and integration conditions are stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Driver 3: acquisitions. The company paid 283,600 (table in thousands) for acquisitions in the nine months, and goodwill rose from 2,143.2 to 2,280.3 (table in millions). Continuing this requires funding capacity and successful integration. Long-term debt rose from 1,169.4 to 1,391.0 (table in millions) over the same period.
quotes: The increase relates to the effects of the Quinnox acquisition, partially offset by older intangibles that have reached the end of their useful lives.

growth_thesis.basis: Management's view is stated in the earnings release and TMT growth in the same release. The sustaining condition is inferred from the 10-K risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: Driver 4: demand for AI and data, cybersecurity, cloud and IT modernization. Management ties its bookings to this demand. In the third quarter, TMT revenue grew 14.6 percent, or 20.0 million, year-over-year. For this to continue, client AI and technology spending must be sustained.
quotes: strong Commercial and Federal bookings reflect continued customer demand for AI and data, cybersecurity, cloud, and IT modernization services

growth_thesis.basis: Margins and net income are stated in the income statement, MD&A and release. The framing as a condition for growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition: growth must convert into earnings. Third-quarter revenue rose, but gross margin fell to 28.3% from 29.4% and net income fell to 23.1 from 38.1 (table in millions). Margin pressure comes from a shift toward lower-margin cloud services, lower permanent placement mix and currency.
quotes: a shift in solutions mix, with stronger growth in certain cloud and infrastructure services that carry lower gross margins than other offerings in our portfolio

growth_thesis.basis: Cash flow and liquidity figures are stated in the cited items. The offering is announced but its completion is not shown. That financing is a condition for growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition: financing and cash generation must support growth. Nine-month operating cash flow was 129,400 against 225,600 (table in thousands), partly because accounts receivable days sales outstanding rose. Revolver availability was about $227.0 million of $600.0 million, and the company announced a $500 million senior notes offering to redeem its 2028 notes.
quotes: announcing its intention to commence a private offering of $500 million aggregate principal amount of unsecured senior notes due 2031

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release. The year-ago fourth-quarter revenue is not in the evidence, so year-over-year growth cannot be read from it.
growth_thesis.claim: Near-term check: fourth-quarter revenue guidance is 965.0 to 995.0 (table in millions), below the third-quarter 1,031.4. The fourth quarter has 61 billable days, 3 fewer than the third. Continued growth depends on results landing within this range.
quotes: The fourth quarter has the lowest number of billable days in the year because of the holidays.

material_events.basis: Announcement is stated in P2. Completion is inferred from the 10-Q's reference to the acquisition's effects on amortization.
material_events.claim: Everforth acquired Quinnox Inc. The deal was announced on January 20, 2026, subject to regulatory approval. The Q3 2026 10-Q later attributes higher amortization of intangible assets to the acquisition, so it appears to have closed. The completion date is not given.
quotes: The increase relates to the effects of the Quinnox acquisition, partially offset by older intangibles reaching the end of their useful lives.

material_events.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release.
material_events.claim: Everforth completed a refinancing and upsizing of its revolver. A new five-year revolving facility of $600 million replaced the previous revolver and Term Loan A.
quotes: On July 7, 2026, completed the refinancing and upsizing of revolver, replacing previous revolver and Term Loan A, with a new five-year $600 million revolving facility

material_events.claim: Everforth announced its intention to offer $500 million of unsecured senior notes due 2031. It plans to use the proceeds, together with revolver borrowings, to redeem in full its 4.625% Senior Notes due 2028. The offering is subject to market and customary conditions.
quotes: announced today its intention to offer $500 million in aggregate principal amount of senior notes due 2031 (the “Notes”), subject to market and customary conditions.

material_events.claim: In fiscal 2025, Federal Government Segment revenues fell because certain contracts were lost as a result of DOGE initiatives. The number and size of the lost contracts are not given.
quotes: Federal Government Segment revenues, which are all consulting revenues, were $1.2 billion, down 3.3 percent year-over-year mainly related to the loss of certain contracts as a result of initiatives associated with DOGE.

risks.basis: Balance sheet and MD&A figures are stated in the items. The strain on liquidity is inferred.
risks.claim: Leverage rose and cash generation weakened: long-term debt was 1,391.0 (table in millions) against 1,169.4 at year-end, nine-month operating cash flow fell to $129.4 million from $225.6 million, and about $227.0 million of the $600.0 million revolver was available.
quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities was $129.4 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with $225.6 million in the same period of 2025.

risks.basis: Figures and drivers are stated. Whether the compression persists is inferred.
risks.claim: Profitability is compressing: Q3 net income was $23.1 million versus $38.1 million a year earlier, and consolidated gross margin was 28.3% versus 29.4%, while Q4 revenue is guided at $965.0 to $995.0 (table in millions) after $1,031.4 million in Q3.
quotes: The fourth quarter has the lowest number of billable days in the year because of the holidays.

risks.basis: Metrics and the termination language are stated. The link to future revenue is inferred, and the filing says there is no assurance bookings become revenue.
risks.claim: Demand indicators softened: federal new contract awards over the trailing twelve months were $1,049.2 (table in millions) versus $1,158.6 with book-to-bill of 0.9 to 1 versus 1.0 to 1, and quarterly commercial consulting book-to-bill was 0.9 to 1 versus 1.0 to 1. Many client agreements can be terminated at will.
quotes: Many of our agreements may be terminated by clients at will and the termination of a significant number of such agreements would adversely affect our revenues and results of operations.

risks.basis: Goodwill, equity and trigger language are stated. Elevated impairment risk is inferred from juxtaposing the market cap and book figures.
risks.claim: A goodwill impairment is possible: goodwill was 2,280.3 (table in millions) against total stockholders' equity of 1,844.0, and the screener shows a marketCap of 1193132958. The filing lists a sustained market-cap decline as an impairment trigger.
quotes: a substantial sustained decline in the market capitalization of our stock

risks.basis: The offering and use of proceeds are stated. The effect on interest cost and covenants is inferred.
risks.claim: Debt refinancing and covenant risk: the company plans a $500 million senior notes offering plus revolver borrowings to redeem its 4.625% notes due 2028. Net interest expense has already risen to $20.2 million in Q3 from $17.4 million.
quotes: Some covenants are tied to our operating results and thus may be breached if we do not perform as expected.

risks.basis: Costs and risk language are stated. Whether the initiatives will underdeliver is not stated and is inferred only as a risk.
risks.claim: Execution risk from strategic initiatives and acquisitions: acquisition, integration and strategic planning expenses were $30.9 million in nine months versus $15.8 million, tied to outsourcing back-office functions, an ERP implementation and Quinnox integration.
quotes: We have recently outsourced, and may further outsource, certain back-office support functions to a third-party vendor in an effort to improve efficiency, strengthen our operations, and capture cost savings.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the cited items for the offering and use of proceeds; the open outcome is inferred from the absence of any pricing or closing disclosure
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the $500 million senior notes offering close, and on what terms, given it is meant to redeem the 4.625% senior notes ($541.0 million outstanding) together with revolver borrowings when only $227.0 million of revolver was available at quarter end?
quotes: The Notes will be general unsecured senior obligations of Everforth.

unresolved_questions.basis: causes stated in the cited items; persistence is not stated
unresolved_questions.claim: Is the gross margin compression from 29.4% to 28.3% structural (permanent placement mix, Mexico currency, cloud mix) or temporary, given Q4 guidance of 28.4% to 28.7%?
quotes: Gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 28.3 percent, a compression of 110 basis points from the third quarter of 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the cited items for the decline and its cause; recovery is unknown
unresolved_questions.claim: Will operating cash flow recover after falling to $129.4 million from $225.6 million in the nine months, a decline management ties mainly to higher receivable days?
quotes: This year-over-year change primarily related to an increase in accounts receivable days sales outstanding in the first nine months of 2026.

unresolved_questions.basis: drivers stated in the cited items; the split among drivers is not stated
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the effective tax rate fall back from 36.5 percent in Q3 toward the 24.6 percent of the prior-year quarter, or stay near the 34.0% assumed for Q4?
quotes: The effective tax rate was 36.5 percent, up from 24.6 percent in the third quarter of 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: guidance stated in the cited item; the year-over-year implication is not determinable from the evidence
unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the step-down in Q4 revenue guidance, $965.0 to $995.0 (table in millions), against Q3 revenues of $1,031.4 million is seasonal billable-day effect versus softer demand? The prior-year Q4 revenue is not in the packet.
quotes: The fourth quarter has the lowest number of billable days in the year because of the holidays.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the screener market cap and balance sheet; the test outcome is not in the evidence
unresolved_questions.claim: Did the annual October 31 goodwill test hold, given goodwill of 2,280.3 and stockholders' equity of 1,844.0 (table in millions) against a screener market cap of 1193132958 (price date Nov 20, zone not stated)?
quotes: For the 2025 impairment test of goodwill and trademarks, the Company performed a qualitative assessment and determined there were no indicators of impairment and it was more likely than not that the fair value of its two reporting units, Commercial and Federal Government, and its trademarks, exceeded their respective carrying amounts.

unresolved_questions.basis: figures and the management statement are stated; the reconciliation between them is inferred as missing
unresolved_questions.claim: How do the management description of strong bookings and the reported Commercial consulting quarterly book-to-bill of 0.9 to 1 (down from 1.0 to 1) and Federal TTM book-to-bill of 0.9 to 1 fit together?
quotes: As we enter the final quarter of the year, strong Commercial and Federal bookings reflect continued customer demand for AI and data, cybersecurity, cloud, and IT modernization services.

unresolved_questions.basis: facts stated in the cited items; the intent behind the pause is inferred and not stated
unresolved_questions.claim: Will share repurchases resume, given none occurred in Q3 while $923 million of authorization remained and revolver availability was $227.0 million of the $600.0 million facility?
quotes: There were no repurchases of the Company's common stock during the quarter; approximately $923 million remained available for repurchases under the Company's stock repurchase plan.

verdict_reason: expected return +10.0 points a year against the required return over 3 years
